gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-stick: Ruler-straight and wide open, Bruno Ace draws its heading in one constant line, while Stick follows in tubelike strokes. Both stay light on the eye.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-suse: SUSE reads friendly and rounded, its bowls tipped open like a ladle toward you. Bruno Ace sits above it, drawn with a ruler and lingering one character per beat.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-suse-mono: SUSE Mono reads plainly, with open curves and extra room on both sides of every letter. Bruno Ace, by contrast, has curves as heavy as its stems, so give the heading a little more size.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-tajawal: Hard-edged and showy, Bruno Ace holds one thick outline from letter to letter. And Tajawal's broad, open-hooked c keeps a longer stretch of sans text moving along smoothly.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-tasa-explorer: Stiff, ruled lines with no brush pressure anywhere. Bruno Ace makes the louder statement up top, while TASA Explorer, a plain sans with curves that lift off like brush strokes, handles the quieter reading below.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-tasa-orbiter: Bruno Ace has a thickness like neon glass tubing, and its counters stay connected to the outside as each character lingers. TASA Orbiter, a plain sans, keeps its tiny counters unclogged.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-teachers: Bruno Ace lingers on each character, one beat apiece, with a ruler-drawn line and counters open to the outside. Teachers, in sans-serif, bends thin steel rod into every letter, so a longer passage feels light and modern.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-telex: Telex is curvy and unclamped, never fussy. Beneath Bruno Ace, whose ruled line has no thick-thin flicker to catch the eye, a long passage of sans text glides along without effort.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-tenor-sans: Ruled and unhurried, Bruno Ace has no tilted stress in its round letters. And Tenor Sans brings light, visible stroke variation, with c tips that never creep toward touching, which is what makes the pair interesting.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-tirra: Bruno Ace draws a marker-like constant line, one character per beat, with counters left open to the outside. Tirra's round forms, like open parentheses, make a longer passage easy going.
